utterances.text: Yes, do that. But prior to that, please answer a couple of questions. First question: Did you see the weapon that was used to fire at you? You said a few moments ago that you were being fired on. Did you see the weapon that was used on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, this is what I saw. The bunker was there in front of the shop, in the direction of the road, leading towards the main road, and direct control of the road so that if you even so much as put your nose out, you would be certainly dead; and if you were not fast enough and ran across this space fast enough, you were in danger of your life.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You mention a bunker. Did you see the weapon which was then used to fire?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: A weapon -- I think that it was a large calibre, not a small arm. It was some sort of Browing, anti-aircraft, a small Browing anti-aircraft weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You have just mentioned a bunker. What do you have in mind? What is, according to you, a bunker?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, sandbags, in fact, piled up one above the other to protect the individual shooting. He would hide behind the sandbags.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How high would those sandbags be piled up?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, they were just the right height so that they could sit down and shoot in chairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: As you suggested, you have behind you an aerial photograph of the village of Ahmici. Would you mind using the pointer to show us where those sandbags, the bunker was, together with the weapon?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, as I showed you -- let me show you exactly so that it's clear to one and all. Look at this. Take a look at this. The road is straight, and only from this point was gunfire able to protect this road and to shoot straight up to this intersection. There is a curvature down here and some houses, but that's not essential. So that is the control point. There is a canal here and a forest there, a thicket. These are the woods, this is the canal (indicating). Is that enough for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I think that it can be noted for the transcript that the witness pointed to the shop in Sutre as being the place the shooting originated from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What time did this firing take place?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: The shooting was about 10.00 in the morning for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Please wait a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It seems to be rather important for you to have the witness indicate from which house the firing was coming. I wonder whether, during the break, you could use the time to present an enlarged photograph without the circles being put on it. So a larger photograph which might be more specific, give us more detail, than this one, which is too big, so that the witness could indicate where the house was. Is that possible during the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I shall look into this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So we will have the break for 30 minutes, as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you mind showing this photograph, this aerial photograph, to the witness? I shall mention to the Court that I did not meet up with the witness during the break, anticipating what might be raised as an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, we have just handed in our decision to the registry - you shall receive it either today or tomorrow morning - a ruling regarding any contacts between one party and its witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph is marked Exhibit 182.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness N, prior to the break, you stated having seen a high-calibre weapon that was behind sandbags. You now see a photograph. Could you, using the pointer, indicate where exactly that weapon was located which was used?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Here in front of this facility (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you take one of the pens lying on the table and could you draw a circle around that location?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 33?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness N, do you recognise and can you identify what is being shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes. On the left-hand side, this building is what I've been talking about, in front of the car. Is that sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Well, it is enough for me. But one more thing to specify. You may have said so already, in which case, please say it again. What time was it when you saw that weapon being used, being fired?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: It was about 10.00, and it was precisely then that I was to pass by, going up towards the hill. I carried a small child. In passing, in the ditch I saw a woman lying who lived behind. I can show you the house in which the woman lived. She was killed. Her daughter was wounded and a relation of mine as well was seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you know how long the firing, originating from that location which you've just shown, how long the firing lasted?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes. They didn't last very long, but they did what they set out to do, they fulfilled the task that they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you have any other recollection from that day, the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, it was hell. The village was encircled, almost under an encirclement. You could only leave from one side but you couldn't during the day. They fired with heavy guns and different ammunition and mortars, fragmentation, weapons, snipers, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When and under which circumstances were you able to leave Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: We succeeded in leaving at about 2.00 p.m. Armoured vehicles came, UN APC vehicles, at 2.00 p.m. came and that was when it was all over, when that hell came to an end, ceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So at the very beginning of the afternoon, you were able to leave Ahmici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Where did you go? In which direction did you go?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness N. I have no further questions for this witness. The only thing I shall ask is that Exhibits 180, 181, and 182 be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can inform you that the witness will be questioned by Counsel Borislav Krajina, Petar Puliselic, Ranko Radovic, and Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Witness, I have three questions to ask you. As they're not long questions, I hope the answers won't be long either. Did I understand you correctly when you said that there was shooting from the bunker that you mentioned and you said that it was located in front of the shop and that this shooting controlled the road from the point where the bunker was located up to the mosque? Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Thank you. My second question: Did you state that from that particular point, they were not able to control the direction towards the forest, the shooting direction towards the forest, and you showed us that on the photograph, on the map?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, not with the weapons that were used to guard the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. That's enough. My third and last question: Would you take this exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit 182 -- could you show this exhibit to the witness, please? -- and could you, Witness, indicate, say place the letter "sh," the suma, the forest that you mentioned and that you said the area which could not be controlled, so a letter "sh," please?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I apologise. You understood me to say that there was just one barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, that's not essential. It's not important. We're not interested in that at the moment. What I'm interested in is for you to show us where the forest is.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: That is the forest, these are the houses along the road, and behind the houses was the forest and the canal (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: What is this to the left-hand side? You went from the mosque downwards. A move forward to the left, what is to the left of the bunker here, in this direction? There is the white surface, and you marked it with a red marker. And then to the left, up above, to the left, there, is that a forest as well? Down below, lower down, two or three centimetres lower down, please. Not up, down, in the opposite direction another centimetre. That. Is that the forest? Don't go up. Stay where I indicated, one centimetre downwards, please. No, you're going up. Down on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: It is difficult to say on this particular photograph what the forest is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: I apologise, but if you want to --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: You're not going to get an answer if you want to trick me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Why should I trick you? I'm not here to trick you.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I am not a minor, I am an adult.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Perhaps counsel could simply ask the witness where the forest is. It seems to be a simpler question, a simpler way of going about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: We're going to mark the forest --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: It's not all a forest, one length of forest, but there are some fields and hills and a ditch, a canal, and so on, so it's not one length of forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, please. On this photograph, we have marked the location of the forest. Can we show this to the witness so that he can tell us whether that is the location of the forest or not? I think that is the simplest method.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I say something for -- let me say something. The forest was cut down later on, so that is something that you must take into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: We're talking, sir, about the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes. There was a forest there then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, then there's no misunderstanding. So I'm going to show you this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: On the photograph, I can't show you the forest now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Because the forest isn't on the photograph any longer. There were trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: I'm going to give you a photograph, and with this circle, we marked the spot which we considered was the forest, and you will tell us whether, on the 16th of April, 1993, there was a forest actually there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, explain to us what a forest is, because in French, a forest is a cluster, quite a solid cluster of trees closely put together. It is quite a large patch of vegetation. So it's very extensive. Is that what Mr. Krajina has in mind? I don't know. There seems to be a misunderstanding. If he would specify what a forest is, maybe that could be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: There is no misunderstanding. We're both Bosnians, myself and the witness, and we understand each other 100 per cent. He is not a Frenchman nor am I a Frenchman. That's as clear as day. So, Mr. President, I'm asking the witness whether that particular place is the forest that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: So will you give us an answer, please? Have you had a look?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes. That is your second photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: It's not our photograph, it is the Prosecution's photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Witness N, do cooperate with the Tribunal and tell Counsel Krajina whether this is the right place, whether the forest is located there. I see you marked -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I'm going to tell you that it is not one length of uninterrupted forest but that there are trees, there is a forest, and then fields and then trees again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, I know Ahmici, I've known Ahmici longer than you have, so would you please show us whether the mark we have made, whether that particular place was a forest or not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: You want to mislead me, you want to trick me, but you are mistaken if you think you're going to be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Krajina is not trying to mislead you. He has just put to you a question, and you should give a straightforward answer. Just tell us whether this is the appropriate mark, whether this mark designates a forest, indicates the forest.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Can I show you on the big picture, on the big photograph, where the forest was and where the fields were, so that everybody can see? Because this is rather dark. Can I, on the big one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: First on the big one and then on the small one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that we can make this, what appears to be a misunderstanding, a little easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Could the witness say whether the spot we have marked with the letter X, to tell us, regardless of whether it's a forest or not, whether, from where the bunker was located, could you control the range of shooting from that point, to control that point?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Will you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Yes. You saw on the photograph what we marked with the X, that particular position, and we said that that was a sort of forest. Now, let's leave the forest alone. What I'm asking you now is, that from the spot where the bunker was located and from the spot that the shooting came from, could this particular spot be controlled, the spot marked with X?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Do you mean the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, not the road. That particular point which is marked X on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, the picture is not very clear. It's unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I withdraw my question. I can't carry on with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to warn you, Witness N, you have to say the truth and cooperate with the Tribunal, so would you please answer the question put to you by Counsel Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I would like to show where the forest was and where the meadow was on the big photograph, and that will be enough for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, no, because Counsel Krajina also put to you a second question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second question. Well, yes, I'll get to the second question too. I will say the following: Later on, they discovered that I was in the former JNA, Yugoslav People's Army. I was doing maintenance and repair work for artillery weapons, and I am quite clear, and the gentleman is quite wrong, if I don't know what can be done with that kind of weaponry from that particular spot. It is special -- they are special weapons which are effective in all directions, a Browing, a Swedish Browing, or something of the kind, a similar name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that from that spot with that particular gun, one could control also the area which has been marked by Counsel Krajina with an X?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of it. Not the whole area on the left. It was the intention that this particular weapon should fire at the road, from which direction civilians were to be taken from the school. One civilian was seriously injured, and somebody will have to pay for that bodily injury, and those kinds of wounds can only be sustained by a heavy weapon, not just a small gun or pistol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Please, Your Honours, Mr. President, again, photograph number 182 be tendered as an exhibit with the mark X which we put on it and nothing more. It was all reduced to a soil configuration, et cetera. We have nothing more to add.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Can I say something? These photographs are different, and why are they different? Why are they different, I ask, this one and that one there? As far as clarity's concerned. As far as clarity's concerned. Well, as far as I can see, they are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution object to tendering this document into evidence? No objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the witness mentions a difference. I didn't quite gather what difference it was. He said the difference between two photographs or the difference between the photograph and reality that he was able to witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: He said the one was clearer than the other, the other one is darker.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: That's what the witness said?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I can show on this photograph in front of me where the forest is and approximately the other configuration, elements, as the other gentleman asked me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand. Do you mean that on the other photographs, you would be able to mark the particular spot, the forest?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: On the large photograph the forest has been felled, and there are only some branches on the spot which can be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Let's go back to this document, and I wonder once again, does the Prosecution have any objection to the tendering of that document into evidence? With the mark, I mean, the photograph marked by --

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit is marked D3/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Krajina. We move on to Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you whether you had made any statements before to anyone else regarding the events in Ahmici. Do you remember that you have given any such statements to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, I never wanted to give any statements, because people ask for money -- rather, they offer money for that, and I did not think myself entitled to something like that, to earn money because of somebody else's misfortune.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But did you make any such statements to any official institutions, to any official bodies?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, to no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: We do have a statement here which you gave to AID. Are you aware of what AID, A-I-D, is, what kind of an organisation?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, I do not know. They should have addressed me. They addressed me and told me what they wanted, and I said no dice, no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this is your signature here. Do you recall that? Do you recall having made any statement?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, I do not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You don't. Okay. You said that you came to Ahmici from a camp. Were you in this camp alone or with your family?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I was there, as well as, normally, the others. And as you are aware, there were seven camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that your family had gone to Austria, and that there had been no room for you there. Was that the only reason why you yourself did not go to Austria, or was there perhaps another reason?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: We talked on the phone, and my sister-in-law said that she was unable to accommodate us all for lack of space, and that she could take in the children, the women and the elderly, and could the not take in the others because she herself was living in another man's house, in somebody else's house, she did not have a flat of her own.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Today here in court, you said that on one occasion you were threatened by Dragan Papic, that you saw him in a black uniform and that on that occasion he threatened you. Can you tell us what was it exactly that he was saying to you while he was threatening you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: He came up to me wearing this uniform and a badge, showed me the badge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But he didn't say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He asked me what my address was, where I was residing, and I didn't want to tell him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you construe that his appearing in that black uniform as a threat?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, but you know why. We, the wretched exiles that we were, we were all down there in the Milicevici's house, and if we were not in that house, we would have ended up like those people who had been expelled from in Foca. And we know how they ended up, they were all killed off. And at the Milicevici's house, they were in charge of that, of executing those people. Only three managed to save their lives -- to flee, rather, because one person who had the necessary paper to be able to move about, the necessary permit, he worked at the bakery in Vitez, he came and told these people to retreat, to pull out, to go away from the cottages, the vacationing cottages where these misfortunate people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I only asked you where this meeting took place, this encounter, when you met with this person that other people told you was called Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: That encounter took place -- there was a prayer going on in front of the mosque. The people go to the mosque in the afternoon and pray to God. Mr. Dragan was then there. I had not seen him ever before that, until today, of course, and since.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you had never seen him before that and you haven't seen him since until today?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was anyone else present when you met him?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, no one else was there, because at that time everybody was in the mosque. There were not any people passing by. There were no passers-by, there were no other citizens present.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Are you quite sure that the person that you indicated here today is the person that you met on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I am a hundred per cent sure, and I know the people that he killed, and he should carry them on his conscience.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: He killed Rasim Pezer, and I knew that man. I let him in Vehbija Ahmic's kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But did you see him kill him?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: And later his father was also killed, and I believe that was also by Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why do you believe that? On the basis of which?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Because I saw him when he was hit. I saw them both when they were hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But in your previous statement you said that you didn't see that, but that you had heard about it, but now you claim that you saw it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I saw them dead. In front of the house where they had been hit I saw some neighbours, I believe they were the Vidovics. They had no weapons, they were just walking in front in the courtyard. And as the shooting died down --

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But how old was this Kasim Pezer?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: He was an elderly man. He was around 60 or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you say that -- whether on the occasion of that meeting with the person who you claim others told you was Dragan Papic, did you see anything conspicuous standing out on his face for instance? Did you see any particular mark on his face which one would normally observe as conspicuous?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I believe that that is a person who is easily induced to do things. I believe that there is something wrong in his behaviour. He sort of winked and there were some tics.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice something on his face?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: He didn't look you straight in the eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but did he wear a beard?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I don't recall whether then he wore a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But you said that you saw some insignia on his uniform, so that you concluded that he was a member of the H-O-S, of the HOS. I believe that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes. It was hard to distinguish and decide who belonged to whom at that time, to what ranks, to what formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but judging by the uniform you said that you concluded that he belonged to the HOS.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: It was difficult to say why, because no one knew who was in command, who was giving the orders. Had that been known, perhaps no such things would have happened, would have been done arbitrarily by people without any commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the HOS cooperated and had joint operations?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes, but that was only a cunning trick. The only thing which mattered was to get the necessary troops. And of course, normally they bought soldiers for money because they also needed to earn a living.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you recall where this meeting took place and what time it was exactly?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: It was noon. It was 12.00. I cannot exactly recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you recall the month?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, I cannot even recall the month, because you know what, if I were able to tell you everything which took place then, I would already be a deranged person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Puliselic. We have two more Defence counsel who wish to cross-examine the witness. We have to stop at five to five. I wonder whether we can finish or probably one of you could probably now go on until five to five? Is that fine? Counsel Radovic, do you think you could -- ten minutes would be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try. I don't think that I have many questions to ask, just en passant.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You said today that you were not included in the Territorial Defence, but that you were on guard duty in front of the mosque; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to AID on the 6th of May '98, you said, "I was included in the Territorial Defence in Ahmici."

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I apologise. It was not Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That's what it states in the statement, TO in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, it was a sort of preventative group. It was nothing in comparison to what they were preparing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that. I just asked whether what you told AID was correct, whether you were included in the Territorial Defence in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, you should know what Territorial Defence means.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know full well what it means because I come from the same area from which you come, and as far as Territorial Defence and the organisation of Territorial Defence, I know everything about it. So please tell me whether you became a member of the Territorial Defence or not, or perhaps you don't remember whether you did or did not.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, there must be guard duty for every facility on every territory, and Territorial Defence, as far as I know, does not win over something belonging to somebody else, but just defends what is theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, were you included in the Territorial Defence to defend what was yours?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Is that important? Is that very important to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I don't know what to do with this witness. If he doesn't wish to answer this particular question, let me go on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any function, any position in the system of defence and social self-protection, which is the term used to refer to that particular job, on the basis of which you would have information as to facts outside your range of vision?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing. I'll tell you exactly. What was important for me at the time was that my children were safe and for me to reach safety, and that was not possible at the time. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether you held any function which would enable you to speak about the facts outside your range of vision.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Nothing, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you, because you spoke about matters that you could not have seen yourself, but it doesn't matter. You spoke about the month of October 1992, and you said that members of the HVO from Busovaca moved towards -- from Busovaca towards Travnik to help the forces at Novi Travnik. How do you know that these individuals who set out on that road were from Busovaca, and how do you know that they were going in the direction of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: This is not an important point.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to assess what is essential and what isn't, I'm just asking you how you know this.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Right. I'll answer you then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, go on then, answer.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I was present when the first conflict broke out. They said that they could not pass and said that we would return from Busovaca, and they returned the next morning with the artillery --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: They told you that they had come from Busovaca. So you were at the barricades there. Very well. Finally I have found somebody who was at the barricades. Where were you at the barricades?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, the barricade was around the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And where were you personally located on this barricade?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, we were --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Don't say "we", because it means more of us. When I'm asking you, I'm asking you personally.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, I was there 30 metres from the barricade where, if you recall, there were entrenched positions, and later on it was decided to destroy these. There was a control and everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And who made up these fortifications?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: The TO, as you say, the TO which was to defend the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, while you were 30 metres from the road in the fortified position of the TO, did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody at the barricade have weapons?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Some of the young men who were included into the army, were members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina beforehand, they were already experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, how many of these experienced young men were there who had weapons and who already knew what war was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, four from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, whether a group from another village came to help you out.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, no help arrived. And when you know everything, then everything becomes quite clear as to the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we know the outcome, but I'm interested to know how it started.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Well, it started because we had one miner killed and several houses burnt, and, therefore, the depression that set in. This person was killed after the barricade had been set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. You mean he was killed before the barricade was set up.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: No, not before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When then? I apologise, Mr. President, but I didn't think that I would take up so much time to go into detail.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: He was killed during the attack from the hill, from the positions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me how the barricades came to be set up? Was it on orders from somebody or was that the will of the people, spontaneously to go down to the road and set up a barricade there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: It is common knowledge that in Novi Travnik the war had already began. Everybody knew this. We knew it from the news bulletins and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you directly. How was the barricade set up? Was there an order from a higher command or not?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I think that an order came from the higher command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And where was this command, from Zenica or from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know where from, because I was not an officer among the ranks of officers for me to know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me, when you found yourself there you said you were 30 metres away from the road. What were you, in fact, doing there? You said that you did not have any weapons, that you did not have any function to perform, so as you went to this position which was in the trenches on the barricade -- Mr. President, I apologise but I won't be able to complete my questioning because we've just started. So should we leave it for tomorrow? I didn't think it would take as long as this?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL SEAN DOOLEY.
utterances.text: Can I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, we've finished. Thank you. We'll continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So we resume tomorrow at 9.30 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
